cards.text: Bildad the Shuhite, one of Job's friends, just told Job that God never perverts justice (Job 2:11; 8:3). Now Job, the man from Uz, answers him (Job 1:1). He starts with "Yes, I know that it is so," and then he turns it into a question.

cards.question: Job agrees with Bildad. Then what does Job ask?

answers.text: How a mortal can be righteous before God
How a mortal can win back all he has lost
How a mortal can win the respect of his friends

cards.text: Then Job pictures someone who wishes to contend with God and take Him on in an argument.

cards.question: Job pictures someone arguing with God. How often does Job say that person could answer Him?

answers.text: Not once in a thousand times
Only on the very first try

cards.text: Job says God is wise in heart. Friend, I can't win an argument with my own oven door, and Job's talking about taking on GOD.

Job starts listing what God does, and friend, this list does NOT slow down. God moves mountains, shakes the earth, commands the sun not to shine, seals off the stars, stretches out the heavens and treads on the waves of the sea.

cards.question: Mountains, the earth, the sun, the stars and the sea. What is Job showing about God with this list?

answers.text: How gently He tends the earth
How He rests after His work

cards.question: Job says God is the Maker of the Bear, Orion and the Pleiades.

cards.text: Job says God does great things beyond searching out, and wonders without number. Meanwhile I've got a few stars lit up in my night sky, and I show them to every baker who walks in like I hung the moon.

cards.question: Job says that if God passed right by him, Job would see Him.
When God takes something away, what does Job say about it?

answers.text: He explains it to you first

cards.question: Job says God holds back His anger.

cards.text: Job says even the helpers of Rahab cower beneath Him, friend. Not argue, not push back: COWER.
Mountains, stars, the sea. With a God like that, Job asks how he could ever answer Him or choose his arguments against Him.

cards.question: Even if Job were in the right, he says he could only beg his Judge for ___.

cards.text: Job says that even if he summoned God and God answered, he doesn't believe God would listen to his voice. And then, friend, Job goes even further: he says God would crush him with a tempest and multiply his wounds without cause.

cards.question: Job says God overwhelms him with bitterness. What does Job say God won't let him do?

cards.text: Job checks every way out. He says, "If it is a matter of strength, He is indeed mighty! If it is a matter of justice, who can summon Him?"

cards.question: Job imagines standing before God. Even if Job were righteous, what does he say would condemn him?
Job says he is blameless.

cards.text: Then Job says it's all the same: "He destroys both the blameless and the wicked." He even says that when sudden death comes, God mocks the despair of the innocent.

cards.question: Job looks at the world around him. Who does he say the earth is given into the hand of?

cards.text: And Job doesn't stop there, friend. He says, "He blindfolds its judges. If it is not He, then who is it?"
Then Job talks about his days. He compares them to a runner, to boats of papyrus and to an eagle swooping down on its prey.

cards.question: A runner, papyrus boats, a swooping eagle. What is Job saying about his days?

answers.text: They are full of good things

cards.text: Job pictures himself deciding to forget his complaint, change his expression and smile. I know that move, friend: I've smiled through a whole burnt batch and told everybody it was "extra crispy."

cards.question: If Job put on a smile, what does he say would still be true?

answers.text: He would still dread all his sufferings
His friends would still walk away from him
His pain would slowly fade on its own

cards.text: Job says that since he's already found guilty, why work for nothing? Then he pictures washing himself with snow and cleaning his hands with lye.

cards.question: Job says washing with snow and lye would get him clean in God's eyes.

cards.text: Job says God is not a man like him, so they can't answer each other or take each other to court. A stamper can take another stamper to court, friend, but who's taking on the One who made the STARS?

cards.question: Job says there's no ___ between him and God to lay a hand on them both.

cards.text: Job says, "Let Him remove His rod from me, so that His terror will no longer frighten me." I'll be honest, friend, I've been scared of a kitchen timer, so I'm not about to tell Job to toughen up.

cards.question: Job says that right now, he's ready to speak to God without fear.

cards.text: Job says, "I loathe my own life; I will express my complaint and speak in the bitterness of my soul." Then he tells what he will say to God.

cards.question: Job tells God not to condemn him. Then what does Job ask God to let him know?

answers.text: How long he has left to live

cards.text: Job asks God straight out if it pleases Him to oppress Job, to reject the work of His own hands and favor the schemes of the wicked. Friend, Job is not holding ANYTHING back.

Then Job asks if God has eyes of flesh, if He sees as man sees, and if His years are like the years of a man. Friend, some mornings I can't see past my own mustache, so I KNOW what eyes of flesh are like.

cards.question: Job asks if God's days are like a man's. What does Job say God is doing to him?
Job says God knows that Job is not guilty.

cards.text: Job remembers how he was made. He says to God, "Your hands shaped me and altogether formed me. Would You now turn and destroy me?"

cards.question: Job asks God to remember that He molded Job like ___.

cards.text: Job says God poured him out like milk, curdled him like cheese and knit him together with bones and sinews. And here I thought getting my name carved on my handle was a big deal.

cards.question: Looking back on how God made him, Job says God has granted him life and that God's care has preserved his spirit.

cards.text: Then Job takes a sharp turn, friend. He says God concealed these things in His heart, and that this was in God's mind: if Job sinned, God would take note and would not acquit him.

cards.question: Job says if he's guilty, woe to him. What does Job say about if he's righteous?

answers.text: He still cannot lift his head
He will be honored by everyone

cards.text: Job says that if he held his head high, God would hunt him like a lion. A LION, friend, and Job is NOT the one doing the hunting.

cards.question: Job says God multiplies His anger toward him and hardships assault him in wave after wave. What is Job saying with that picture?

answers.text: His troubles keep coming one after another
His troubles will soon wash away for good
His troubles are smaller than they look

cards.text: Then Job asks God why He brought him from the womb, and he wishes he had been carried from the womb to the grave. Friend, I know something about the dark from my years in the junk drawer, so I'm just going to sit with this one quietly.

cards.question: Job says his days are few, and he asks God to come closer to him.
Job describes the place he's headed as a land of light and rest.

cards.text: That's where Job leaves it, friend, in the dark. But hold on, because this story is a long way from over.
